dedupe_keys.name: palm model system with palm 4u urban climate components

description: PALM is a turbulence-resolving large-eddy simulation model of atmospheric and oceanic boundary layer flows, built for massively parallel computers (tested up to 32,000 cores, with GPU support), that can also run in a cheaper RANS mode. Its PALM-4U components, shipped with the model, serve urban applications from meso to micro scale with city-wide or district coverage: buildings are resolved on a Cartesian grid down to 1 m or finer, with energy balance solvers for buildings and paved surfaces, radiative transfer in the urban canopy with shading and multiple reflections, a wall material model, an indoor climate module giving indoor temperature, energy demand and waste heat, a chemistry module, self-nesting, a multi-agent system of residents for biometeorology, and forcing from COSMO-DE, ICON or WRF. It is developed at Leibniz University Hannover with a community of research groups and described in Maronga et al. (2020) for version 6.0. The code is accessible from the project's GitLab release repository as free software under GNU GPL v3, with documentation being moved to a new site and training through the PALM Academy launched in August 2026. Caveats: runs at building scale need high-performance computing and detailed urban input data, and the documentation is in transition. It supports simulation of urban heat, ventilation and green and blue infrastructure options in city planning for climate adaptation; related records are UMEP and the Stuttgart green ventilation corridors case study.
